Definition: middle voice from G2041; to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc.:--commit, do, labor for, minister about, trade (by), work.
BiblicalUsage: Ergázomai means to work — to toil at a task, to labour with your hands. Paul works with his own hands so as not to burden the churches, and he tells the Thessalonians to work quietly and eat their own bread. It is honest labour, and Scripture treats it as a duty, not a curse.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ergázomai dignifies ordinary work: God gave it before the Fall, and He still blesses the hands that do it. I hold that working with my own hands is part of my witness, not a distraction from it.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
